title: Conditional reflected-moment contraction
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product space, and let $q,c\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<q$ and $0\le c\le1$. Suppose that $|1-cz|^q\le |1+z|^q-q(1+c)z$ for every real $z$. Then the product expectation of $|E_Jf-c(f-E_Jf)|^q$ is at most the product expectation of $|f|^q$, where $E_J$ denotes conditional expectation over coordinates outside $J$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with positive coordinate weights summing to one
$f$ is real-valued on the product space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $J\subseteq[n]$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $q>0$, and $0\le c\le1$. If $|1-cz|^q\le|1+z|^q-q(1+c)z$ for every real $z$, then $\mathbb E_P|E_Jf-c(f-E_Jf)|^q\le\mathbb E_P|f|^q$.
